finding: _update_list relabels an OSError raised by the transform's marker work as a list-file failure
why: The try wraps update_locked, which runs transform inside; add and repoint call _claim_folder there, whose marker.read_bytes, folder.iterdir and safe_write._replace_if_unchanged (temp open, fsync, os.replace) can raise OSError, so a failure on <root>/<name>/.afk-repository is reported as 'repositories.json: cannot be read or written' and the real path is lost.
fix: Wrap only the update_locked I/O, not the transform: catch OSError inside _claim_folder and _release_folder and raise RepositoryListError naming the folder or marker (as the mkdir case at repo_list.py:348 already does), or have transform wrappers convert before the outer catch.
evidence: repo_list.py:383-385 `safe_write.update_locked(list_file(), transform)` / `except OSError as error: raise RepositoryListError(f"cannot be read or written ({error})", list_file())`; transform calls _claim_folder at :148, :201; _claim_folder does unwrapped `folder.iterdir()` :338, `marker.read_bytes()` :351 and marker write :354. Failing input: root folder exists but is read-only/ACL-denied for writing -> PermissionError from os.open of the temp marker -> message names the list file.

finding: remove's release catch still lists OSError, which _update_list can no longer raise
why: After this change every OSError out of _update_list is already a RepositoryListError, so the OSError arm is dead and hides that _release_folder's own OSError (iterdir, unlink at :363-366) now arrives as a list-file RepositoryListError.
fix: Drop OSError from the tuple (or keep it deliberately with a comment); no behavior change.

finding: The blanket OSError catch also relabels marker and folder I/O errors as a list-file failure
why: The catch wraps the transform too, so an OSError from _claim_folder's marker.read_bytes / folder.iterdir / safe_write._replace_if_unchanged (lines 338, 351, 354) surfaces as 'cannot be read or written' with list_file() as the target, naming the wrong file.
fix: Catch OSError only around the list-file open/lock, or have the transform wrap its own marker and folder OSErrors in RepositoryListError naming the folder, as line 348 already does for mkdir.
evidence:
except OSError as error:
        raise RepositoryListError(f"cannot be read or written ({error})", list_file()) from error  (wraps safe_write.update_locked(list_file(), transform), whose transform runs _claim_folder, repo_list.py:351-354)

finding: dangling-link test does not assert the link survives the write
why: The test is named 'written through' but only checks target.is_file(); a writer that replaced the link with a regular file at the list path would still pass.
